label: Game A
nuance_found: Tower defense on a sandwich plate: pick between toothpick (fast single), pickle cannon (splash), mustard (slow cone); stack toppings (tomato damage, cheese speed, lettuce range, bacon burn) with rising prices; burners via FLAME to roast olives; SWAT to finish the Jar boss. Stovetop needed cannons plus splash coverage at the corners and saving coins for wave 7-9, but one build (cannons plus toppings) is clearly best.
audio: Looping upbeat music that changed between stages and a victory jingle, plus thwips, pops, cannon booms, placement plops and wave dings; sound was constant and satisfying.
furthest_progress: Level 1 Cutting Board cleared with 3 stars (score 10,200); level 2 The Stovetop lost twice at wave 7 and wave 9/10, then beat on the 4th try incl. The Jar boss at wave 10 for 1 star (score 18,690, 3 bites left); The Sink unlocked but not played.
control_trouble: Menu stays open after building so my blind chained taps sometimes missed a build or closed a panel; occasionally had to redo a placement. Not the game's fault.
best_moment: The Jar boss lumbering to my sandwich with 3 bites left and the 'SWAT it!' prompt saving it.
worst_moment: Stovetop wave 7 spike: 60+ olives and losing at wave 9/10 twice with no hint of what to change.
verdict: Right away I knew what to do: tap a circle, build a sandwich weapon, olives pop with good squelchy sounds and +3 coins flying. It looks like a finished Royal Match style game and levels have stars and orders to chase. The second level got hard fast and I lost twice, which on the bus would nearly make me quit, but I was close each time so I tried again and the boss fight felt like a real payoff. I would keep this and play again this week.
